blockMcqs.question: What single factor separates aggregation from composition?
options: Number of methods in the class
Whether the part's lifetime is independent of the whole
Whether the classes are in the same file
blockMcqs.explanation: Aggregation's part can outlive the whole; composition's part is destroyed with it.

blockMcqs.question: Which best describes association between two classes?
options: One class creates and destroys the other
A peer link where both can exist independently
One class extends the other's type
A link that vanishes when a method returns
blockMcqs.explanation: Association is a loose 'uses-a' link; neither side owns the other.

blockMcqs.question: In aggregation, what happens to the part if the whole is destroyed?
options: It can continue to exist independently
It becomes part of another whole automatically
blockMcqs.explanation: Aggregation gives the part an independent lifetime, so it survives the whole.

blockMcqs.question: Which pattern signals composition rather than aggregation?
options: The part is passed into a constructor from outside
The whole creates the part internally with 'new'
The part is stored in a global registry
The part implements an unrelated interface
blockMcqs.explanation: Composition typically builds the part inside the owner, tying its life to the owner's.

blockMcqs.question: House-and-Room is a textbook example of which relationship?
blockMcqs.explanation: Rooms have no meaning outside their house and are destroyed with it — composition.

blockMcqs.question: Department-and-Professor is a textbook example of which relationship?
blockMcqs.explanation: A professor can move to another department, so the lifetime is independent — aggregation.

blockMcqs.question: A method takes an object as a parameter but never stores it. What relationship is this?
blockMcqs.explanation: No stored field means the link is temporary — dependency, not association.

blockMcqs.question: A Car is-a Vehicle and has-a Engine. Which pairing is correct?
options: Car-Vehicle is inheritance, Car-Engine is composition
Car-Vehicle is composition, Car-Engine is inheritance
blockMcqs.explanation: Is-a maps to inheritance; has-a with exclusive ownership maps to composition.

blockMcqs.question: In UML, a filled (solid) diamond at the whole end represents which relationship?
blockMcqs.explanation: A solid diamond marks composition's exclusive, dependent ownership.

blockMcqs.question: Why is 'inherit just to reuse fields' considered a design smell?
options: Inheritance is always slower at runtime
It creates a false is-a relationship instead of has-a
Subclasses cannot have fields of their own
It requires more memory than composition
blockMcqs.explanation: Reusing fields via inheritance without true substitutability misuses is-a; composition fits better.

blockMcqs.question: In the pseudocode, why is Department-Professor aggregation, not composition?
options: Professor objects are created outside and passed in via addProfessor
Department stores professors in a dashed line
blockMcqs.explanation: The professor is built independently and only added afterward, so it can outlive the department.
